data.title: Macron welcomes Canada's Carney to French Atlantic territory
data.description: SAINT-PIERRE - French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday welcomed Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney to France's tiny North Atlantic territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, just off the Canadian coast.

data.title: Germany's Merz under pressure after bruising state election losses
data.description: BERLIN - German Chancellor Friedrich Merz starts the week more damaged than ever after his centre-right CDU party suffered two bruising regional election defeats at the hands of far-right and far-left parties.

data.title: Malaysia's 'elephant whisperer' fights to save Borneo's endangered giants
data.description: SUKAU, Malaysia - Deep in Malaysia's Borneo jungle, wild shouts fill the air as a Bornean elephant is darted and her angry herd rallies to protect her.

data.title: Thousands march in France against 'licence to kill' draft law
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Thousands of people marched in Paris and other French cities on Sunday against a proposed law on the legitimate use of force that critics say would be a "licence to kill" for police and gendarmes.

data.title: 'I live in fear': 1.5 million Pakistani children sexually exploited online
data.description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistani teenager Zara Shah was targeted by a stranger while playing a computer game, drawn into a conversation that would expose her to terrifying online sexual exploitation.

data.title: Top US, Chinese economic officials meet ahead of Trump-Xi summit
data.description: NEW YORK - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng began talks Sunday, as they set the stage for possible agreements on trade, AI and other issues before a summit of the countries' top leaders.

data.title: US warns of rapid escalation in Mideast war
data.description: RIYADH (SAUDI ARABIA) - The United States warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis could "escalate rapidly" after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed.

data.title: Russians vote on last day of parliamentary elections
data.description: MOSCOW - Russians headed to the polls on Sunday for a third and final day of tightly controlled parliamentary elections set to strengthen the Kremlin's grip on power, as the Ukraine war grinds through its fifth year.

data.title: Hong Kong customs seizes record B533m marijuana shipped by sea from Thailand
data.description: HONG KONG - Customs has made the largest seizure of drugs shipped by sea in Hong Kong's history, discovering HK$125 million (533 million baht) worth of marijuana in a 40-foot container and arresting three people.

data.title: Hong Kong customs seizes record B533m worth of marijuana shipped by sea from Thailand
data.description: HONG KONG - Customs has made the largest seizure of drugs shipped by sea in Hong Kong's history, discovering HK$125 million (533 million baht) worth of marijuana in a 40-foot container and arresting three people.

data.title: German state elections threaten new shock waves for Merz
data.description: BERLIN - German voters go to the polls Sunday in two state elections where far-right and far-left gains could send new shock waves to Berlin and rock the government of embattled Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

data.title: Leo XIV, first US pope transcends his restrained style
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Prudent yet conciliatory, Pope Leo XIV has gradually imprinted his style on the leadership of the Catholic Church, finding his voice as he takes on some of the world's most pressing issues, from bloody conflicts to artificial intelligence.

data.title: Packing for a pope: behind the scenes on foreign trips
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Papal trips mean vast crowds, high-level diplomatic meetings and a formidable amount of behind-the-scenes preparation, from delicately balanced agendas to complex security protection for the head of the Catholic Church.

data.title: Pope Leo in France: the issues on the table
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Pope Leo XIV is set to begin an official visit to France on September 25, with several thorny issues hanging over the trip, from clerical sexual abuse to the country's new assisted dying law.

data.title: Chile's Bachelet quits race to be next UN chief
data.description: SANTIAGO (CHILE) - Michelle Bachelet, the former president of Chile, withdrew her candidacy for the position of United Nations secretary-general on Saturday, weeks after a straw poll showed her in second to last place among eight candidates.

data.title: 'It has to stop': runners protest women's murders in S.Africa district
data.description: KEMPTON PARK (SOUTH AFRICA) - Hundreds of runners gathered Saturday in South Africa's Kempton Park, near Johannesburg, where the body of a 38-year-old mother was discovered earlier this month -- one of nine woman to be murdered in the district in two months.

data.title: Cuba works to restore power after another blackout
data.description: HAVANA - Cuba worked Saturday to restore power after its seventh major blackout of the year, as the communist-run island grappled with woes triggered by a US fuel blockade.

data.title: France's debt climbs to highest since 1978: ministry
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France's debt mountain is growing and will this year be at its highest level since 1978 because of a soaring deficit, the country's finance ministry said Saturday.

data.title: CNN, MS NOW denied access to White House grounds
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US media outlets CNN and MS NOW said they were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday, a day after President Donald Trump announced a ban against them for reporting what he calls "fake news."

data.title: Saudi capital issues air raid alert
data.description: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia - Saudi authorities issued their first air raid alert in the capital since fighting returned to neighbouring Yemen, leaving residents of Riyadh rattled after they heard explosions ringing out in the early hours of Saturday.

data.title: Malaysian minister resigns to protest Najib pardon
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - The ​leader ‌of Malaysia’s Democratic Action Party (DAP) said ​on Saturday that he would resign as ⁠transport minister over a Pardons Board decision ​to allow house arrest for former ​prime minister ‌Najib Razak.

data.title: Russia reports online attacks on voting system
data.description: MOSCOW - ⁠Russian ⁠authorities reported multiple attacks ​on voting systems and communication lines across ​the country on ‌Saturday, the second day of three days of voting in a parliamentary election.

data.title: Trump signs bill to impose sweeping Russia sanctions
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump signed a bill on Friday authorising new sanctions designed to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine, after Congress gave its approval after months of delay.

data.title: Western Australia beaches closed after fatal shark attack
data.description: ‌Several beaches along the coast of Western Australia, including in the state capital Perth, will remain closed until at least Sunday, authorities said, after a ​fatal ⁠shark attack at a popular beach in the city on Friday.

data.title: Death toll from attack at police HQ in Pakistan rises to 31
data.description: KOHAT, Pakistan - The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan rose to at least 31, including 16 police personnel, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday, with fighting ongoing.

data.title: Nigerian miners struggled to breathe in cell before 37 died: survivors
data.description: MINNA, Nigeria - Survivors of a Nigerian disaster in which 37 suspected illegal gold miners died while in the custody of a paramilitary civil defence group recounted their panic on Friday as they struggled to breathe inside the cell.

data.title: Drone owners rush to offload gear ahead of Beijing ban
data.description: BEIJING - Drone owners in Beijing flocked to designated buy-back sites this week, looking to sell their devices for as much as possible ahead of an impending citywide ban.

data.title: Helicopters battle wildfire threatening Ecuador's capital
data.description: QUITO - Ecuadoran firefighters backed by helicopters on Friday battled a major blaze on a hill overlooking the capital Quito that has led to the evacuation of dozens of people.

data.title: 'Pause' on overt repression in Venezuela, but reforms still needed: HRW
data.description: CARACAS - Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has overseen a "pause" in the overt repression of opponents since taking office in January, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said Friday, 18 years after the organization was expelled from the country.

data.title: Trump claims 'infinite' Greenland security deal with Denmark
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had struck a deal with Denmark to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security that would bar Russia and China from setting up bases in the Arctic territory.
